newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian prime minister to take finance portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Latvian prime minister to take finance portfolio.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele will also take the post of finance minister in his new government, politicians said on Thursday.
"The minister of finance will be Andris Shkele," Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs told reporters.
Shkele decided to take the finance portfolio after earlier rejecting the candidacy of the head of Latvia's largest party for the post.
Shkele's government is due to be put to the vote by parliament later on Thursday.
The finance minister's post has been controversial and was the cause of the fall of Shkele's previous administration.
Shkele resigned in January after President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament to reject Shkele's choice of finance minister, which has been a vacant post since October.
Ulmanis made the call after reports the proposed finance minsiter Vassily Melnik had been investigated by the prosecutor's office.
Melnik was confirmed by parliament but later resigned.
Shkele and Ulmanis also settled their differences and the president recalled Shkele to the premier's post after a week.
